title: Kestrel and the Extraction
premise: Silas Eastwick, a veteran air-crash investigator, has spent six years hiding the truth about Flight 4471 — the maintenance log he altered to protect a whistleblower who never survived to testify. When the remote safe house sheltering him and his estranged daughter Mara is listed online with interior photos, the people who silenced the whistleblower find them within seventy-two hours. Hunted across the Scottish Highlands by a fixer named Corven and betrayed by the handler who built their cover, Silas must decide whether to trade his secret for their lives or release it publicly and destroy the airline, the regulator, and himself. In the end, Mara — not Silas — chooses justice: she broadcasts the log from her father's own evidence kit as Corven closes in, buying their survival at the cost of everything Silas spent years protecting.
about_author: Ines Thackeray is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading crash reports before turning to fiction. She writes from a croft on the Moray coast, where the weather does half her plotting for her.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At a memorial for Flight 4471's victims, Silas recites his polished lie about that night while privately rehearsing the escape routes he's memorized for six years. Introduces his go-bag, his guilt, and the distance between him and Mara. Emotional beat: grief worn like a uniform.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Bored and resentful in the safe house, Mara finds their home on an estate agent's site — interior photos including Silas's locked evidence case on the kitchen table. She confronts him; he lies badly. Emotional beat: the first crack in the wall between father and daughter.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He calls handler Ruth Calloway, who dismisses it as a database error but quietly activates extraction. Silas packs the go-bag and finally tells Mara a partial truth: they're leaving tonight. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Corven
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. The fixer Corven reviews the listing photos, recognizes the evidence case's distinctive latches, and mobilizes a three-man team. Cold, procedural, almost tender about his work. Emotional beat: menace without malice — just a job.

chapters.title: The Road North
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A night drive through the Highlands toward a new safe house; Mara tests her father's story and catches contradictions. They argue about her mother, who died believing Silas's version of the crash. Emotional beat: anger as intimacy.

chapters.title: Safe House Two
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The replacement house is wrong — sightlines too open, one road in. Silas's investigator instincts scream while Ruth insists protocol is protocol. He rigs tripwires anyway. Emotional beat: professional paranoia vindicated by instinct.

chapters.title: What Silas Altered
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Silas's POV. Six years earlier: the whistleblower's call, the falsified inspection record, the crash, and Silas's choice to edit the log rather than hand over a dead man's name. Emotional beat: the origin of the lie, told with terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A 'meter reader' appears at the gate; Mara photographs him and sends the image to a number her mother left her — an old contact of Silas's. First sign someone outside the official chain might help. Emotional beat: agency discovered.

chapters.title: Ruth's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Pressured from above to close the Eastwick file permanently, Ruth realizes she's being used as bait. She must choose between the service that made her and the man she once loved. Emotional beat: duty curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Breach
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Corven's team hits Safe House Two at 3 a.m.; Silas's tripwires buy ninety seconds. Father and daughter flee into freezing rain with only the go-bag. Emotional beat: terror, then the strange calm of survival mode.

chapters.title: The Bothy
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sheltering in a derelict shepherd's bothy, Mara demands the whole truth. Silas gives it — the log, the alteration, the name he protected. Emotional beat: confession as the first honest thing between them in years.

chapters.title: The Name
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The whistleblower was not alone; there is a second copy of the unaltered log, hidden where only Silas can find it. He realizes Ruth may already know. Emotional beat: hope arriving wrapped in suspicion.

chapters.title: Hunted Ground
chapters.summary: Corven's POV. Tracking through the hills, Corven loses a man to the terrain and grows impatient with his employers' insistence that the log be recovered intact, not destroyed. Emotional beat: the hunter noticing the leash.

chapters.title: Old Frequencies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The number her mother left reaches Eilidh Brand, a retired journalist who covered 4471. She agrees to meet — but warns that everyone who helped the whistleblower is dead or scattered. Emotional beat: fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Calloway's Confession
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth intercepts Silas and Mara, admits she leaked the safe house under orders, and offers them a way out if they surrender the log. Silas refuses; Mara watches her father choose principle over safety. Emotional beat: betrayal met with an unexpected offer.

chapters.title: The Cache
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Retrieval of the second log from a lockbox in a decommissioned signal station — the same station where the whistleblower made his final call. Corven's team arrives early. Emotional beat: triumph interrupted mid-breath.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Station
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cornered, Silas negotiates: the log for their lives. Corven, learning his employers plan to kill everyone including him, hesitates. Mara secretly films the exchange. Emotional beat: the deal that isn't a deal.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. While Corven escorts them out, Mara uploads the log and her footage using the signal station's old transmitter rig — her mother's idea of a legacy. The file goes live. Emotional beat: a daughter finishing what her parents started.

chapters.title: Everything Burns
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The broadcast detonates: arrests, resignations, the airline's shares collapsing. Corven, exposed, makes his own choice and lets them walk — then vanishes. Ruth is taken into custody, still protecting someone above her. Emotional beat: victory that feels like loss.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Public inquiry. Silas testifies to his own alteration, accepting prosecution, and names every name he kept for six years. Mara sits in row twelve of the gallery — deliberately. Emotional beat: accountability chosen freely.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The verdict: a reduced sentence for cooperation. Father and daughter speak through glass about ordinary things — weather, food, her plans. Emotional beat: love rebuilt on truth instead of protection.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, eighteen months later. Released early, Silas joins Eilidh's investigative unit; Mara has finished her mother's unfinished report. On the moor above the old safe house, they watch a kestrel hover — holding position against the wind, going nowhere, seeing everything. Emotional beat: survival as a practice, not an ending.
